sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary + Investment Thesis**

ICICIBANK's subsidiaries demonstrated robust growth in fiscal 2025, with notable performances from ICICI Lombard General Insurance, ICICI Prudential Asset Management, and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance. The net premium earned by ICICI Lombard General Insurance increased by 8.3% year-on-year to ₹268.34 billion, while its profit after tax rose to ₹25.08 billion. ICICI Prudential Asset Management's profit after tax increased to ₹26.48 billion, driven by higher income from operations and other income. ICICI Prudential Life Insurance witnessed a 15.7% growth in Annualised Premium Equivalent to ₹104.7 billion. The Bank's overall performance was also strong, with the profit after tax increasing to ₹11.89 billion. 

Our investment thesis is centered around ICICIBANK's diversified business model, with a strong presence in insurance, asset management, and banking. The Bank's ability to maintain a majority shareholding in ICICI Prudential Asset Management post-listing is a positive, as it will continue to benefit from the growth of its subsidiaries. With a total capital adequacy ratio of 18.5% at ICICI Bank Canada and 22.6% at ICICI Bank UK, the Bank's international operations also demonstrate a strong capital position. We believe that ICICIBANK's diversified revenue streams, robust growth in subsidiaries, and strong capital position make it an attractive investment opportunity. However, a detailed peer comparison is not possible due to the lack of available data.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body:
**Business Overview + Segment Breakdown**

ICICI Bank's business operations are diversified across various segments, including Retail Banking, Wholesale Banking, Treasury, and Other Banking, among others. As per the guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on AS 17 – Segment Reporting, the Bank has reported its business segments accordingly. The Retail Banking segment includes exposures that satisfy the four criteria of orientation, product, granularity, and low value of individual exposures for retail exposures. The Wholesale Banking segment comprises advances to trusts, partnership firms, companies, and statutory bodies, which are not included under Retail Banking. The Treasury segment primarily includes the entire investment and derivative portfolio of the Bank.

The Bank's segment breakdown also includes Life Insurance, General Insurance, and Others, which comprise various subsidiaries such as ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited, ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited, and ICICI Home Finance Company Limited, among others. The Unallocated segment includes items such as tax paid in advance net of provision, deferred tax, and provisions to the extent reckoned at the entity level. The results of reported segments for the year ended March 31, 2025, are not comparable with that of reported segments for the year ended March 31, 2024, due to the consolidation of new entities and discontinuation of certain entities from consolidation. Unfortunately, the filing excerpts do not provide a detailed breakdown of the revenue or profit contribution of each segment, making it challenging to analyze the performance of each segment.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body:
The financial performance of ICICI Bank and its subsidiaries for the fiscal year 2025 has been notable, with several key highlights. The net premium earned by the insurance subsidiaries increased, with ICICI Lombard General Insurance witnessing an 8.3% year-on-year rise in Gross Domestic Premium Income to ₹268.34 billion. The profit after tax for ICICI Lombard General Insurance also increased from ₹19.19 billion in fiscal 2024 to ₹25.08 billion in fiscal 2025, primarily due to an increase in net earned premium and investment income. Similarly, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance saw a 13.2% increase in total premium earned, reaching ₹489.51 billion, and a 15.7% increase in Annualised Premium Equivalent to ₹104.7 billion.

The bank's other subsidiaries also reported significant financial performances. ICICI Prudential Asset Management's profit after tax increased from ₹18.15 billion in fiscal 2024 to ₹26.48 billion in fiscal 2025, driven by an increase in income from operations and other income. ICICI Securities' consolidated profit after tax rose from ₹17.33 billion to ₹17.52 billion, primarily due to an increase in net interest income and fee income. ICICI Home Finance's profit after tax increased from ₹5.32 billion to ₹5.56 billion, driven by an increase in net interest income and fee income. However, peer comparison is not possible due to the absence of relevant data. Overall, the financial performance of ICICI Bank and its subsidiaries reflects a positive trend, with increases in key revenue streams and profitability across various business segments.

sections.title: Key Financial Ratios
sections.body:
The 'Key Financial Ratios' section of this report is limited due to the absence of comprehensive financial data in the provided excerpts. However, we can derive some insights from the available information. For ICICI Bank Canada, the total capital adequacy ratio stood at 18.5% as of March 31, 2025, compared to 17.8% in the previous year. Similarly, ICICI Bank UK reported a total capital adequacy ratio of 22.6% at March 31, 2025, down from 23.3% in the previous year. The net impairment ratio for ICICI Bank Canada increased to 0.46% at March 31, 2025, from 0.24% in the previous year, while ICICI Bank UK saw a decrease in its net impairment ratio to 0.2% from 1.1% in the previous year.

To calculate the return on assets (ROA) for ICICI Bank Canada, we can use the profit after tax and total assets. Given that the profit after tax for ICICI Bank Canada was ₹4.35 billion in fiscal 2025 and total assets were CAD 5.23 billion (approximately ₹3,143.69 crore, assuming 1 CAD = 60.33 INR, though the exact exchange rate is not provided), we can derive the ROA as follows: ROA = ₹4.35 billion / ₹3,143.69 crore ≈ 0.014 or 1.4%. However, please note that this calculation involves an assumption about the exchange rate and may not reflect the actual ROA. Unfortunately, without more detailed financial information, such as revenue from operations, net profit, and net worth, we cannot calculate other key financial ratios like return on equity (ROE) or debt-to-equity ratio. Peer comparison is also not possible due to the lack of peer data in the provided excerpts.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of ICICI Bank highlighted the strong performance of its subsidiaries, which contributed to the increase in consolidated profit after tax from ₹442.56 billion in fiscal 2024 to ₹510.29 billion in fiscal 2025. Notably, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company, ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company, ICICI Securities Primary Dealership, and ICICI Home Finance Company all reported higher profits, offset partially by declines in ICICI Bank Canada and ICICI Bank UK. The consolidated assets of the Bank and its subsidiaries grew from ₹23,640.63 billion at March 31, 2024, to ₹26,422.41 billion at March 31, 2025, driven by an increase in consolidated advances from ₹12,607.76 billion to ₹14,206.64 billion over the same period.

The Bank's capital adequacy ratios remained robust, with a consolidated Tier-1 capital adequacy ratio of 15.81% and a consolidated total capital adequacy ratio of 16.41% at March 31, 2025, exceeding the regulatory requirements of 9.70% and 11.70%, respectively. The management's focus on diversifying revenue streams and improving profitability across its subsidiaries has yielded positive results, with ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company and ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company reporting significant increases in profit after tax to ₹26.48 billion and ₹25.08 billion, respectively, in fiscal 2025. However, without peer data, it is not possible to conduct a comparative analysis of ICICI Bank's performance relative to its industry counterparts.

sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The Key Risks section of this report highlights the potential challenges that ICICI Bank may face, as outlined in its Annual Report for the year ended March 31, 2025. The bank has identified several risks that could impact its operations and financial performance, including statutory and regulatory changes, international economic and business conditions, and political or economic instability in the jurisdictions where it operates. Additionally, the bank is exposed to risks such as an increase in non-performing loans, unanticipated changes in interest rates, foreign exchange rates, equity prices, or other rates or prices. The bank's growth and expansion in business, adequacy of its allowance for credit losses, and exposure to market risks are also potential areas of concern.

These risks are further detailed in the bank's filings with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission, which are available at www.sec.gov. The bank's Risk Committee, which met six times during the year, is responsible for reviewing the bank's risk management policies pertaining to credit, market, liquidity, operational, outsourcing, model risk management, and framework for early warning signals and red flagging of accounts. While the bank has implemented various measures to mitigate these risks, they still pose a potential threat to its financial performance and operations. As of the report date, the bank has not provided specific financial metrics or quantitative data on these risks, and therefore, a detailed analysis of their potential impact on the bank's financials cannot be provided.

sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
Recent Developments

ICICI Bank has made notable developments in its subsidiaries and associates during the financial year ended March 31, 2025. On March 24, 2025, the Bank increased its stake in ICICI Securities Limited from 74.34% to 100.00%, resulting in the entity becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Bank. In terms of financial performance, ICICI Bank Canada's profit after tax decreased from ₹4.50 billion in fiscal 2024 to ₹4.35 billion in fiscal 2025, primarily due to a decrease in core operating profit. ICICI Bank UK's profit after tax also decreased marginally from ₹2.39 billion in fiscal 2024 to ₹2.27 billion in fiscal 2025, primarily due to a decrease in core operating profit. 

In the insurance segment, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance (ICICI Life) reported a 15.7% increase in Annualised Premium Equivalent to ₹104.7 billion for fiscal 2025, and a 6.4% increase in the Value of New Business (VNB) to ₹23.70 billion for fiscal 2025. The total premium earned by ICICI Life increased by 13.2% to ₹489.51 billion in fiscal 2025, while the total assets under management increased from ₹2,941.40 billion at March 31, 2024 to ₹3,093.59 billion at March 31, 2025. These developments indicate the Bank's continued expansion and growth in its various business segments.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The 'Bull vs Bear vs Base Case' section of our report on ICICI Bank Limited (ICICIBANK) presents three possible scenarios for the company's future performance. The bull case is supported by the strong performance of ICICI Bank's subsidiaries, with ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited reporting profits after tax of ₹25.08 billion and ₹11.89 billion, respectively, in fiscal 2025. Additionally, ICICI Securities Limited (consolidated) reported a profit after tax of ₹17.52 billion, indicating a stable and growing securities business. These positive trends could lead to increased revenue and profitability for ICICIBANK, driving the stock price upwards.

In contrast, the bear case is driven by potential risks and uncertainties, including statutory and regulatory changes, international economic and business conditions, and an increase in non-performing loans. These factors could negatively impact ICICIBANK's growth and expansion, leading to decreased revenue and profitability. The base case scenario assumes a steady-state environment, with ICICIBANK's subsidiaries continuing to perform in line with their historical trends. As per the filing excerpts, ICICI Bank Canada reported a profit after tax of ₹4.35 billion in fiscal 2025, while ICICI Bank UK PLC reported a profit after tax of ₹2.27 billion. These numbers indicate a stable performance by the bank's international subsidiaries, supporting the base case scenario. Overall, our analysis suggests that while there are potential risks and uncertainties, the strong performance of ICICIBANK's subsidiaries and stable international operations provide a positive outlook for the company's future performance.

Business Segments Pursuant to the guidelines issued by RBI on AS 17 – Segment Reporting, the following business segments of the Group have been reported. i. Retail banking includes exposures of the Bank which satisfy the four criteria of orientation, product, granularity and low value of individual exposures for retail exposures as per RBI guidelines. This segment also includes income from credit cards, debit cards, third party product distribution and the associated costs. ii. Wholesale banking includes all advances to trusts, partnership firms, companies and statutory bodies, by the Bank which are not included under Retail banking. iii. Treasury primarily includes the entire investment and derivative portfolio of the Bank. iv. Other banking includes leasing operations and other items not attributable to any particular business segment of the Bank. Further, it includes the Bank’s banking subsidiaries i.e. ICICI Bank UK PLC and ICICI Bank Canada. v. Life insurance represents results of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited. vi. General insurance represents results of ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited. vii. Others includes ICICI Home Finance Company Limited, ICICI Venture Funds Management Company Limited, ICICI International Limited, ICICI Securities Primary Dealership Limited, ICICI Securities Limited, ICICI Securities Holdings Inc., ICICI Securities Inc., ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company Limited, ICICI Prudential Trust Limited, ICICI Investment Management Company Limited, ICICI Trusteeship Services Limited, ICICI Prudential Pension Funds Management Company Limited and I-Process Services (India) Private Limited. viii. Unallocated includes items such as tax paid in advance net of provision, deferred tax and provisions to the extent reckoned at the entity level. Income, expenses, assets and liabilities are either specifically identified with individual segments or are allocated to segments on a systematic basis. All liabilities of the Bank are transfer priced to a central treasury unit, which pools all funds and lends to the business units at appropriate rates based on the relevant maturity of assets being funded after adjusting for regulatory reserve requirements. The transfer pricing mechanism of the Bank is periodically reviewed.
